title: Flowers That Hold a Memory
paras: On the [[outskirt|outskirts]] of a small coastal town, paper maker Leila Nasser turns flowers into sheets of writing paper. Customers bring wedding bouquets or flowers from a relative's garden, hoping to preserve a connection with someone important. Leila began this work after discovering that her grandmother's dried roses had started to [[rot|rot]] in a damp cupboard.

Her workshop opens onto a stone [[patio|patio]], where she removes each flower from its [[stem|stem]] and separates the petals. The petals are dried, then mixed into pale paper pulp. To [[simplify|simplify]] the choices for customers, she offers only three paper sizes. However, she allows [[unlimited|unlimited]] revisions to the short handwritten message that accompanies each order. 'People often know what they feel before they know what to say,' she explains.

The business requires more than patience with emotions. A part-time [[bookkeeper|bookkeeper]] checks every [[debit|debit]] on the workshop's bank statement, while Leila's cousin comes twice a week to [[assist|assist]] with packing. Last winter, the [[installation|installation]] of a drying cabinet allowed her to work during wet weather. Previously, several days of rain could delay an order by a fortnight.

Leila does not promise that every flower will keep its original colour. Instead, she sends customers a small sample before making the final sheets. One man initially disliked the grey traces left by his mother's yellow flowers. Later, he ordered more paper: the faded marks reminded him of her gardening coat. For Leila, that unexpected recognition matters more than perfect preservation.
zh: 在一座海滨小镇的郊外，造纸手艺人莱拉·纳赛尔将鲜花制成书写纸。顾客带来婚礼花束，或是亲人花园里的花，希望留住与重要之人的情感联系。莱拉发现祖母的干玫瑰在潮湿的柜子里开始腐烂后，便开始了这项工作。
她的工作室通向一处铺着石板的庭院，她在那里将每朵花从花茎上取下，再把花瓣分开。花瓣晾干后，被混入浅色纸浆。为了让顾客更容易选择，她只提供三种纸张尺寸。不过，每份订单附带的简短手写留言，都可以不限次数地修改。她解释道：“人们往往先明白自己的感受，之后才知道该如何表达。”
经营这门生意，所需要的不只是耐心体察他人的情绪。一位兼职记账员核对工作室银行账单上的每笔扣款，莱拉的一位堂亲或表亲则每周来两次，协助包装。去年冬天，安装了一台烘干柜后，她在潮湿天气里也能工作了。在此之前，连续几天下雨就可能让订单延迟两周。
莱拉不承诺每朵花都能保持原来的颜色。她会在制作最终的纸张前，先寄给顾客一小份样品。一位男士起初不喜欢母亲那些黄花留下的灰色痕迹。后来，他又订了更多纸张：那些褪色的印记让他想起母亲做园艺时穿的外套。对莱拉而言，这种意想不到的情感共鸣，比完美保存花朵更有意义。

q.s: Leila's grandmother's dried roses had been stored for ten years before they began to rot.
q.why: 首段未说明干玫瑰腐烂前保存了多久。

q.s: Customers can change their accompanying message only three times.
q.why: 留言修改次数不限，三种指纸张尺寸。

q.s: Installing a drying cabinet enabled Leila to work during wet weather.
q.why: 第三段说明安装烘干柜后她可在潮湿天气工作。
